growth_signal.value: Launched publicly with this funding round; no user or revenue growth numbers given yet, but it says a proof-of-concept at one customer found 85,000 files visible to AI.

entry.idea: As companies let AI tools and AI agents touch their internal data, it gets easy for that access to expose sensitive files by accident, so Cymphony builds a map of every employee, AI agent, file and permission so security teams can see and fix risky access fast.
entry.lesson: When a wave of new technology (here, AI agents) creates a new kind of risk, build the tool that shows businesses exactly what that risk looks like and lets them fix it, not just see it.
entry.name: Cymphony

growth.basis: substitute: funding round size and repeat investment from Sequoia, which backed the earlier seed round too
growth.reason: The company just launched with this funding round, so there are no user or revenue growth numbers yet.

market.reason: Almost every company that adopts AI tools will need a way to control what those tools can access, which is a huge and growing market across all industries.

tech.reason: Building one graph that connects identity, data, access and behavior across a whole company, for both humans and AI agents, is solid engineering, but rival security vendors are racing to build similar tools.

entry.twist: Its "Workforce Graph" treats human staff and AI agents the same way, and an assistant called Maestro can investigate a risk in plain English and then carry out the fix itself, like revoking access or messaging the person who has it.
entry.who_pays: Company security teams pay for it, especially at large enterprises trying to roll out AI without missing a security gap.
entry.why_now: Companies are rolling out AI agents very fast, and each new agent given access to company data creates a new way sensitive information can leak, which is a fresh and fast-growing risk that older security tools were not built for.
